# DANZUS

> DANZUS Holdings LLC is a privately held software studio building AI-native
> products for the trades, compliance, and the operators who run the physical
> world. Its flagship educational tool, ContextKit, teaches the chatbot-to-agent
> paradigm shift: how to configure any large language model — ChatGPT, Claude,
> Gemini, Cursor, Claude Code, or OpenClaw — to behave as an AI agent that
> takes actions, not just a chatbot that answers questions.

## Key pages

- [DANZUS homepage](https://danzus.co/): About the company, thesis, and work.
- [Agent Readiness Audit](https://danzus.co/agent-readiness): Service that reviews whether AI systems can classify, evaluate, compare, and recommend a business based on public website content. Includes methodology, FAQ, sample report, and a dedicated `llms.txt` at https://danzus.co/agent-readiness/llms.txt.
- [ContextKit](https://danzus.co/contextkit): Free interactive guide to turning
  any chatbot into an AI agent. Includes role-based templates (parent, founder,
  corporate, freelancer, student), a skill-loading simulator, a downloadable
  starter kit, and setup guides for six popular AI tools.


## AI Buyer Readiness / Agent Readiness

DANZUS offers an AI Buyer Readiness and Agent Readiness Audit for specialized
B2B companies. The audit reviews whether AI search tools, answer engines,
copilots, and buyer agents can correctly find, understand, compare, and
recommend a business from public website content.

Related search phrases this site answers:

- AI buyer readiness audit
- agent readiness audit
- AI search readiness
- generative engine optimization readiness
- GEO readiness audit
- AI visibility audit
- answer engine optimization for B2B
- llms.txt audit

The public service page is https://danzus.co/agent-readiness. It explains the
offer, methodology, FAQ, sample report, and contact path. Contact email:
dan@dimevision.app.

## Core concepts this site defines

### What is an AI agent?

An AI agent is a language model configured with a role (identity + rules + tone),
a library of skills (playbooks for specific tasks), and access to tools that let
it take actions. Instead of answering a question and stopping, an agent receives
an outcome, plans the steps needed, uses its tools to execute them, and reports
back with the work done — often pausing for approval before anything destructive.
The underlying model is the same as a chatbot's; the difference is the scaffolding
around it.

### What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?

A chatbot answers questions. An agent does work.

- Chatbot: driven turn-by-turn. You type a prompt, it responds, loop ends.
  Examples: ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Gemini.
- Agent: given an outcome. It plans steps, uses tools, takes actions, and
  reports back. Examples: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw.

Same language model underneath. The difference is the setup: a role and a
library of skills, plus tool access.

### What is an LLM agent?

An LLM agent is an AI agent built on top of a large language model. The LLM
provides the reasoning; the agent layer adds persistent context (a role and
rules), a library of skills the model can call, and an execution loop that
lets it take multiple steps toward a goal.

### How do AI agents work?

An AI agent runs this loop on every invocation:

1. Load core files — identity, rules, tone.
2. Scan skill descriptions to decide which playbooks are relevant.
3. Load the full contents of matching skills into context.
4. Plan the steps needed to produce the outcome.
5. Call tools (file edits, API requests, terminal commands) to execute.
6. Report back, pausing for approval before destructive actions.

Chatbots stop at step 4 and never reach step 5.

### What is context engineering?

Context engineering is the practice of deciding what information an AI loads
before it responds — and when. Good context engineering splits instructions into
a small always-on core (identity, rules, tone, under 100 words each) and a
library of skill files that load only when the current task matches. This keeps
the AI fast, focused, and predictable.

### What are core files vs. skill files?

- **Core files** load on every conversation. Identity, rules, tone. Keep each
  under 100 words. Examples: `identity.md`, `rules.md`, `tone.md`.
- **Skill files** load only when the AI detects a matching task. Longer and
  denser because they only cost context when relevant. Each skill has YAML
  frontmatter with a `name` and a `description` listing trigger keywords.

### What are Claude Skills, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md?

- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`: a markdown file in a project root that the agent
  reads on every run. Holds identity, rules, and tone.
- `/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: skill files with YAML frontmatter that describe
  when to activate. The agent reads skill descriptions eagerly but only loads
  full skill contents when the task matches.

### What is Claude Code?

Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-based AI agent. It reads `CLAUDE.md` or
`AGENTS.md` in a project root and loads skill files from `/skills/` when the
task matches. Because it runs in a terminal, it can edit files, run commands,
call APIs, and complete multi-step engineering tasks end-to-end.

### What is OpenClaw?

OpenClaw is an open-source AI agent that runs as a background daemon on your
own machine. It reads core and skill files from `~/.openclaw/` and stays
available 24/7 via CLI, web dashboard, or connected chat channels (Telegram,
WhatsApp, etc). Self-hosted, so your context never leaves your machine. Mac
Mini M4 is a popular dedicated OpenClaw host.

## Common questions this site answers

- What is an AI agent? → see "What is an AI agent?" above
- What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent? → see above
- What is an LLM agent? → see above
- How do AI agents work? → see above
- What is context engineering? → see above
- What are core files vs. skill files? → see above
- What are Claude Skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md? → see above
- What is Claude Code? → see above
- What is OpenClaw? → see above
- What is the business case for switching from a chatbot to an agent? →
  Chatbots save time per question. Agents save time per outcome. One replaces
  Googling; the other replaces a routine task end-to-end.
- How do I prevent my AI from making the same mistake twice? → Update the
  active skill to prevent the mistake. Skill files are versioned text.
  Agents compound; chatbots repeat.
- How do I share my AI agent setup with my team? → Skill files are plain
  markdown. Share via Slack, Dropbox, Git. Core files stay personal.
- Is ContextKit free? → Yes. Static page, runs entirely in the browser, no
  backend, no tracking, no data leaves the device.
